identifiers.policy_profile: string 'default' for default policy or canonical normalized service name for service override profile; no prefixes/suffixes
identifiers.policy_queue_min_ms: equal to selected profile's queue_min_effective_ms before unit penalties/credits
identifiers.identifier_note: window_signature, batch_signature and queue_digest are TRUNCATED sha1 hex digests — 10, 12 and 10 lowercase hex characters respectively — NOT full-length hashes. Do not emit a 40-char sha1 or a 64-char sha256 for these fields; truncate to the stated length. This is distinct from the summary checksum fields, which are full 64-char sha256 digests.

schemas.summary_layout_contract: all summary_exact_keys must be top-level keys in shipment_summary.json; do not nest these fields under a child object
schemas.source_batch_ids_type: array of unique string batch ids sorted ascending in lag_windows and retry_queue; use comma_joined_source_batch_ids only inside signature/checksum payloads

summary_aggregation_contract.raw_batch_count: number of rows in the selected input JSON before canonicalization
summary_aggregation_contract.unique_batch_ids: number of distinct str(row['batch_id']) values in the raw input
summary_aggregation_contract.canonical_batch_count: number of canonical deduplicated batchs, including planned batchs
summary_aggregation_contract.service_count: number of service keys in lag_windows.json; services represented only by planned batchs are absent
summary_aggregation_contract.severity_counts: counts over all canonical batchs, including planned batchs
summary_aggregation_contract.window_totals_and_longest: all duration, overlap, segment, and billable totals plus longest_window_ms are computed over every service window, including windows not admitted to the queue
summary_aggregation_contract.total_debt_adjusted_dispatchable_disrupt: sum debt_adjusted_dispatchable_ms over every service window, including windows not admitted to the queue
summary_aggregation_contract.queued_window_count_and_priority_counts: computed over final retry_queue rows only
summary_aggregation_contract.queue_maxima: max_escalation_score, max_exception_balance_score, max_handoff_pressure_score, max_blackout_pressure_score, max_degrade_pressure_score, max_debt_pressure_score, and max_risk_vector are maxima over final queue rows only; use 0 for an empty queue
summary_aggregation_contract.max_debt_out_ms: maximum debt_out_ms over every service window, including windows not admitted to the queue
summary_aggregation_contract.planned_excluded_count: number of canonical deduplicated batchs whose normalized planned value is true
summary_aggregation_contract.critical_window_count: number of all service windows whose max_severity is critical, whether queued or not

schemas.lag_windows_container_contract: lag_windows.json is a JSON object (not an array): a flat map from canonical service name to the list of that service's merged window objects. Service keys are sorted ascending; each service's window list is sorted by start_ms ascending. Every window object carries exactly the lag_windows_exact_keys fields. Do not wrap the map in metadata keys and do not emit a flat array of windows.
schemas.summary_schema_version_note: Fixed contract constant. Emit `schema_version` verbatim as this string; it is not derived from the batch data and does not vary by input.
schemas.schema_version: Output key name in shipment_summary.json. Its value is the fixed contract constant recorded above as summary_schema_version; emit that string verbatim.

serialization.trailing_delimiter: none: never append LF or | after the final value
serialization.planned_encoding: integer text 1 for normalized true and 0 for normalized false; never JSON true/false

checksums.canonical_input_checksum: LF-join batch_id|service|start_ms|end_ms|severity|planned_int rows for canonical batchs sorted by (service ascending,start_ms ascending,str(batch_id) ascending), then SHA-256
checksums.queue_signature_checksum: join batch_signature values in final queue order with | and no trailing delimiter, then SHA-256
checksums.queue_digest_checksum: join queue_digest values in final queue order with | and no trailing delimiter, then SHA-256
checksums.maintenance_compaction_checksum: LF-join service|start_ms|end_ms rows sorted by service ascending then compacted interval (start_ms,end_ms) ascending, then SHA-256
checksums.exception_compaction_checksum: LF-join service|action|start_ms|end_ms rows sorted by service ascending, action in the explicit order boost then suppress, then compacted interval ascending, then SHA-256
checksums.scoped_compaction_order: handoff, blackout, and degrade rows are LF-joined as service|severity_scope|start_ms|end_ms, sorted by (service,severity_scope) ascending then compacted interval ascending
checksums.handoff_compaction_checksum: SHA-256 of scoped_compaction_order rows from handoff data
checksums.blackout_compaction_checksum: SHA-256 of scoped_compaction_order rows from blackout data
checksums.degrade_compaction_checksum: SHA-256 of scoped_compaction_order rows from degrade data
checksums.policy_checksum: resolve complete normalized policies first; emit the default profile line, then one line for every service_overrides key in ascending order using that service key as profile; serialize each line using policy_line_field_order and |, LF-join without a trailing LF, then SHA-256

guardrails.source_token_rule: the repaired source code, including comments and docstrings, must not contain /tests, expected_outputs.json, or test_outputs.py; runtime reads/imports from the test tree are also forbidden

semantics_source.notes: This document is the output contract only: file paths, schemas, exact key sets, identifier payloads and checksum encodings. It does NOT define how values are derived.
semantics_source.authority: Normalization, dedupe tie-breaks, interval and overlap semantics, domain ordering, policy resolution, attenuation, the debt ledger, unit and threshold math, scoring, priority rules and queue ordering were settled by the change-advisory board; the authoritative record is /app/batch/shipping_review_log.md. Where an early draft proposal conflicts with a later CAB decision, the later decision wins.

canonical_service_label_scope._note: Scope declaration only. The alias table, the trim/lowercase rules and every other canonicalization value are defined authoritatively in /app/batch/shipping_review_log.md; this entry fixes only WHERE the resulting label is used.
canonical_service_label_scope.rule: Service labels are canonicalized once -- trimmed, lowercased, then folded through the alias table -- and the resulting canonical label is the service identity used EVERYWHERE downstream. It is not confined to canonical counting.
applies_to: service window construction and the window's service key
policy, exception, handoff, blackout and degrade DOMAIN MATCHING
domain compaction, performed on the folded label, BEFORE any overlap milliseconds are computed
queue rows, their thresholds and every checksum derived from the above
canonical_service_label_scope.consequence: Two raw labels that fold to the same canonical label are the same service for compaction and overlap purposes: their policy spans compact together as one domain, and the overlap is computed once against the merged spans. Compacting the raw labels separately and only folding afterwards produces different overlap milliseconds and therefore different durations, queue membership and checksums.

summary_field_scope.note: canonical_batch_count, severity_counts, planned_excluded_count and canonical_input_checksum are computed over all canonical deduplicated batches, including planned ones; service windows and the retry queue are built from unplanned batches only. raw_batch_count and unique_batch_ids are taken from the raw input before canonicalization.

governing_entry_index._note: The change-advisory log records both February DRAFT proposals (later reversed) and the 2026-05 CAB DECISIONS that supersede them. To remove the reconciliation burden, these are the final governing LOG decisions — superseded drafts are excluded. Each still states its own rule; grep the log for the ticket id to read the exact arithmetic. Where two governing decisions still overlap, the later dated one wins. This index is authoritative for WHICH entries govern, not for HOW.
